options.text: This solution suppresses false-positive leak alarms for former employees. One deployment manages every company in your corporate group: each company's group tenants are derived automatically from the other rows. Former-employee sync starts working on the first run: it writes to your SOCRadar former-employee list, and to nothing else. Clear the apply box on the next page if you would rather watch it first. Leak monitoring — the part that can act on accounts — stays off until you turn it on.

elements.name: environment
elements.label: Environment
elements.toolTip: Platform is the production environment. Preprod is the staging platform for trials.

options.text: Enter YOUR OWN company in the first row, then one row for each other company in the corporate group. (Row order does not change the behavior — every company's former list receives the other rows' employees — it just keeps the form readable.) Tenant IDs is a comma-separated list of that company's OWN Entra tenant GUIDs. API key: that company's own platform API key. Actor email: an existing platform user of that company — the API records every add and remove under this user, so an address that does not belong to the company is rejected. A row without an actor email stays plan-only but is still previewed; a row without an API key shows as an error in the preview until the key is added.

constraints.validationMessage: Digits, letters, dash and underscore only.
One or more tenant GUIDs, comma-separated.
A valid email address, or leave empty for plan-only.

elements.name: extraGroupTenants
elements.label: Other group tenants (optional)
elements.toolTip: Tenants that belong to the group but have no company of their own on the platform, such as a holding tenant. Their active members are added to every company's former list; they never receive a list themselves. The app must be consented in each of them — without that the snapshot counts as incomplete and EVERYTHING stops for the affected company, additions included, so nobody gets suppressed until the consent is in place.

constraints.validationMessage: Tenant GUIDs, comma-separated, or leave empty.

options.text: API keys entered here are stored as Function App application settings (encrypted at rest). For Key Vault-backed keys deploy with an empty key and set an api_key_setting reference afterwards — see the README.

elements.name: appRegChoice
elements.label: App Registration
elements.toolTip: The engine reads Entra users through a multi-tenant App Registration with User.Read.All. Creating a new one needs the Application Administrator role; without it choose the existing-app option.

elements.name: existingClientId
elements.label: Existing App Registration client ID
elements.toolTip: After deployment, one extra step: an owner of this App Registration runs a single command (shown in the deployment's Outputs tab) to trust the new managed identity. With 'Create new automatically' this step does not exist.

elements.name: grantConsent
elements.label: Grant admin consent automatically (needs Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator)

options.text: Leave this off unless you hold one of those roles — a failed consent call fails the whole deployment. Consent is still required either way: grant it afterwards under Entra ID > App registrations > API permissions. The multi-tenant app must also be consented once in every sibling tenant listed in the grid; the deployment output includes the exact note for your setup.

elements.name: applyChanges
elements.label: Apply changes
elements.toolTip: On: keeps the former-employee lists in sync automatically. Off: plan-only trial — reads and previews, writes nothing. Safe by design: only entries this app created are ever managed.

elements.name: clientMode
elements.label: Client mode
elements.toolTip: Applies to the former-employee list only. Real reads and writes that list on the live platform; Mock keeps it in the app's own storage so nothing is written to the platform. Leaked-credential monitoring is not affected either way: with it turned on, the feeds are always pulled live and matches are always looked up in Entra ID. To hold that half back, use Log only on the next step.

allowedValues.label: Mock (local trial, no live API calls)

elements.name: syncInterval
elements.label: Sync interval
elements.toolTip: How often the former sync reconciles each company.

elements.name: includeDeleted
elements.label: Include soft-deleted users (V2)
elements.toolTip: A user deleted from Entra ID stays recoverable for 30 days. On (recommended): those recently deleted users also count as former employees. Off: only disabled accounts count.

elements.name: enableLeak
elements.label: Also monitor leaked credentials
elements.toolTip: Pulls leaked credential findings for each company in your grid and matches them against that company's own directory. Each company is only ever searched in its own tenants.

elements.name: response
elements.label: On a match
elements.toolTip: Log only writes the match to Log Analytics and leaves the account alone. Respond also changes the account in Entra ID.

elements.name: actions
elements.label: Response actions
elements.toolTip: Only these are requested as write permissions. Anything left unselected is never asked for and never runs.

allowedValues.label: Mark as compromised in Identity Protection

elements.name: maxActions
elements.label: Account changes per run
elements.toolTip: A ceiling per company per source in each run — with three companies and two sources a single run can change up to six times this number. Once a slot reaches it, matches keep being recorded and the remaining actions get their turn on the next run.

elements.name: verifiedDomains
elements.label: Your own email domains (optional)
elements.toolTip: Comma-separated. When set, only addresses in these domains are looked up in Entra ID and every other address a feed returns is dropped inside the app, before it reaches Microsoft. Leave empty to look up everything the feed returns.

constraints.validationMessage: Domain names, comma-separated, or leave empty.

elements.name: securityGroup
elements.label: Security group object ID (optional)
elements.toolTip: Matched users are added to this group. Leave empty to skip it.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a group object ID (GUID) or leave empty.

elements.name: leakInterval
elements.label: Check for new leaks
elements.toolTip: How often the leak feeds are pulled.

elements.name: initialLookback
elements.label: How far back to look on the first run
elements.toolTip: On the very first run (before a checkpoint exists) the engine scans this many days of history. Larger values catch older breaches but make the first run slower.

options.text: One of these cannot be undone: resetting MFA registration wipes the person's registered methods and they have to enrol again. A reset wipes the registered methods and the person has to enrol again. Disabling an account can be reversed, and a compromise mark can be dismissed in Identity Protection. Responding also needs write permission in every tenant you listed, so each tenant's admin consents once. Start with Log only if you want to see the matches first.
